route: response-frequency matching per item (route 9, item axis) + published totals/alpha/correlations (route 3); option direction by subscale-criterion polarity
evidence: Route 9 on the item axis + route 3. Positional reconstruction of the PLOS S1 workbook's 20 '@12' columns (1-based 48-67) against irw_fetch: 80 of 80 item x resp-level count cells identical (e.g. UPPSP_16 179,152,122,41 live = 179,152,122,41 source; UPPSP_12 10,68,315,101 = 10,68,315,101), and all 20 source count-vectors are DISTINCT, so the match separates every item from every other item. Header-embedded number equals position for 19 of 19 numbered headers. Corroboration: the raw sum of exactly those 20 columns equals the workbook's own pre-computed 'SUPPSP' total for 494/494 respondents; Cronbach's alpha 0.834 vs the paper's published 0.834; r with the workbook's EESR/CESD/DERS totals +0.382/+0.422/+0.473 vs the paper's published +0.382/+0.422/+0.473. PARTIAL, not VERIFIED, because these routes pin the item CODE to its source COLUMN and 19 of those columns carry their own wording, but they establish NEITHER (a) UPPSP_1's words -- its header is the block instruction with the item label truncated to 'I', so the canonical SUPPS-P sentence was placed by elimination on the scoring key (the 19 labelled headers cover all four items of every facet except perseverance, of which only {4,7,11} are present) and only corroborated by correlation (largest correlate UPPSP_11 at +0.535; mean +0.367 with {4,7,11} vs +0.147 with the other 16) -- NOR (b) the option labels, whose DIRECTION is established (negative-urgency sum r=+0.537 with the study's depression total, positive urgency +0.479, premeditation -0.074, so 4 = strongly agree, the reverse of the paper's parenthetical) but whose WORDING for levels 2 and 3 is unpublished and ships blank.

route: 3 (published reliability per construct) + 1 (per-item factor loadings, weak) + explicit code labels in the paper
evidence: Check against the study's own S1 File (CC BY 4.0, sha256 5aabb592951f0b0bff81eab1baeb0203fce733c461bdf8f04a495758eea4504e), re-runnable as verify_yang_2023_green_brand_image.R. BLOCK IDENTITY (route 3): Cronbach's alpha recomputed per letter block reproduces all six of the paper's Table 3 alphas to 3dp -- A .807 vs .80748, B .779 vs .77891, C(C1,C2,C4) .712 vs .71195, D .743 vs .74331, F .849 vs .84915, E .934 vs .93354; largest deviation .00048. So the four blocks shipped here are the four brand-image dimensions, and the nearest rival construct alphas (.849, .934) are missed by .137 or more. C4 IDENTIFICATION: the paper prints the third social-image item as C3 and the raw file has no C3 column; alpha{C1,C2,C4}=.71195 reproduces the published three-item .712 exactly, while every two-column subset is far off ({C1,C2}=.5753, {C1,C4}=.6070, {C2,C4}=.6767), so the published factor cannot be two of these plus an unobserved C3 and C4 is the item Table 1 labels C3. WITHIN-BLOCK ORDER (route 1, weak): one-factor ML loadings per block are A .678/.774/.846, B .705/.744/.758, C .588/.688/.743, D .742/.810/.573 against Table 3's published A .789/.838/.838, B .809/.799/.797, C .743/.781/.785, D .795/.800/.737 -- the published rank order is reproduced in C (3/3) and D (3/3) and is consistent in A, but reverses in B. NOT ESTABLISHED: the published loadings are the authors' full-CFA values and do not reproduce numerically (deviations up to .157), and two blocks publish near-tied loadings (A2=A3=.838 exactly; B1/B2/B3 span .012), so no route separates items within a block. The order of items WITHIN each of the four blocks rests on Table 1's explicit code labels alone -- and this paper's code labels are known to slip once (C3 vs C4). The option_text<->resp axis is also unverified: the 1=disagree / 5=agree direction comes from the methods sentence alone. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

route: 3 (published reliability per construct) + 1 (published standardized factor loadings) + explicit code labels in the paper
evidence: Two-part check against the study's own S1 File (CC BY 4.0, sha256 5aabb592951f0b0bff81eab1baeb0203fce733c461bdf8f04a495758eea4504e, 341 rows), re-runnable as verify_yang_2023_perceived_value.R. BLOCK IDENTITY (route 3): Cronbach's alpha recomputed per letter block reproduces all six of the paper's Table 3 alphas to 3dp -- A .807 vs .8075, B .779 vs .7789, C(C1,C2,C4) .712 vs .7119, D .743 vs .7433, E .934 vs .9335, F .849 vs .8491; largest deviation .0005. So this table's E1-E3 block is the 'Consumption intention' factor (alpha .934) and NOT 'Customer perceived value' (.849, missed by .085), which is what the table name asserts and the shipped instrument name contradicts. WITHIN-BLOCK ORDER (route 1): the just-identified one-factor standardized loadings on E1/E2/E3 are .940/.961/.825 against Table 3's published .893/.896/.836; rank order agrees exactly (E3 < E1 < E2). LIVE TIE: irw_table_sets(per_item=TRUE) gives live n = 341/341/341 for E1/E2/E3, equal to the S1 File's non-missing 1-5 counts of 341/341/341 for the same three columns. NOT ESTABLISHED: the loading pattern separates E3 (lowest in both, .836 published / .825 observed) from {E1,E2} but does NOT separate E1 from E2, whose published loadings differ by .003; within that pair the mapping rests on Table 1's explicit E1/E2/E3 code labels, and this paper's code labels slip once (Table 1 prints C3 where the raw file's column is C4). The per-item n are identical at 341 across all three items, so they tie the block to the live table but distinguish no item from another. The option_text<->resp axis is not tested at all -- the paper names only the two endpoints (1 = disagree, 5 = agree). Hence PARTIAL.
